process_area.title: Customer Take-Back Operations — Collection, Handling & Reverse Logistics

value_stream.name: Household Hazardous Waste, Paint & Used-Product Stewardship Take-Back Program

fields.Participants: HSE Officer, Paint Dept Supervisor, Reblending Partner
fields.Trigger: Customer returns leftover paint at the take-back counter

workflows.name: Customer Paint Take-Back, Latex/Oil Sorting & Usable Paint Reblending (PaintCare)

Automation Opportunity: - Barcode/label scan auto-classifies paint type from the merchandise master (links VS-01/VS-137) and logs to the ledger.
Controls: - CTL-179: return-fraud detection — water-filled containers; CTL-171 (paint hazardous-waste handling).
Cross-references: - links to VS-09 (paint dept/mixing), VS-13 (loyalty), VS-114 (DG containment)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mis-sort risk**: oil-based paint routed to the latex reblending batch contaminates it and ruins the reblended product; mitigated by sort-at-counter SOP and a separate cabinet section per type.
- **Fume/fire risk**: accumulated solvent-based paint in an unventilated cabinet creates fume/fire exposure; mitigated by ventilated flame cabinet and quantity caps per the BFP FSIC.
System Touchpoints: - Take-back transaction record (per customer, per container); hazardous-waste ledger (paint stream); loyalty incentive (VS-13).
Time Estimate: - ~6 min per visit; ~5,000/yr/store at a busy store → ~500 person-hours/yr/store.

steps.activity: Verify eligibility/quantity per policy (W5350); inspect container (labeled, not mixed with other waste).
Sort by type: water-based (latex/acrylic) vs. oil/solvent-based; separate non-paint (thinners, stains) to the solvent stream (W5357).
Stage in the ventilated flame cabinet (W5349); log container count/volume to the store hazardous-waste ledger.
Issue loyalty points/incentive per policy (W5350).
Flag usable volumes for reblending/donation (W5362) vs. recycling/disposal.

fields.Participants: HSE Officer, Oil Re-refinery Partner, Store Receiving

workflows.name: Used Motor Oil, Lubricant & Filter Collection & Bulk Consolidation

Automation Opportunity: - Drum fill-level sensor auto-schedules pickup before capacity; liters auto-logged via flow meter.
Controls: - CTL-792 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Take-Back Operations — Collection, Handling & Reverse Logistics (PA-187.2).)
- operational: used-oil hazardous-waste handling; CTL-21 (volume-accuracy on the ledger).
Cross-references: - links to VS-114 (DG), VS-24 (HSE/spill), VS-61 (fleet oil cross-link), VS-175 (propane/gas adjacency)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Contamination risk**: coolant/solvent/fuel mixed into used oil makes it un-re-refinable and hazardous; mitigated by a verification/refusal step and customer guidance.
- **Spill risk**: a drum overflow or spill contaminates the store/site (Clean Water Act RA 9275); mitigated by bunding, fill-level monitoring, and spill kits.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste ledger (used-oil stream, liters); drum fill-level tracking; bulk pickup scheduling (W5360).

steps.activity: Verify the container is used oil/lube only (no coolant/solvent/fuel mixed — refusal script if contaminated).
Transfer to the bunded oil-rated drum in the containment area (W5349); log liters to the ledger.
Drain/collect used oil filters into a separate rated container; log count.
Issue incentive per policy (W5350).
Monitor drum fill level; schedule bulk consolidation pickup before capacity (W5360).

fields.Participants: HSE Officer, Battery Recycler Partner, BFP Fire Safety
fields.Trigger: Customer returns used batteries (auto, power-tool, appliance, electronics)

workflows.name: Lead-Acid & Lithium Battery Collection, Safe Storage & Fire-Separation Compliance

Automation Opportunity: - Chemistry auto-suggested from the merchandise master barcode; suspect-cell isolation checklist.
Controls: - CTL-792 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Take-Back Operations — Collection, Handling & Reverse Logistics (PA-187.2).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-114 (DG), VS-24 (HSE/fire), VS-179 (EPR/e-waste), VS-143 (appliance take-back cross-link)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Thermal-runaway/fire risk**: a damaged/swollen lithium cell short-circuits and ignites in the containment area — a severe retail fire (BFP, life safety); mitigated by terminal-taping, fire-separated non-conductive bins, and a quench-container isolation procedure.
- **Acid-leak risk**: a cracked lead-acid battery leaks acid in the containment area; mitigated by acid-rated containment and spill kits.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste ledger (battery stream by chemistry); fire-alarm/suppression integration; recycler-partner scheduling (W5360).

steps.activity: Identify chemistry: lead-acid (auto/UPS) vs. lithium-ion (power tools/electronics) — distinct fire/storage profiles.
Inspect for damage/swelling/leak; tape terminals of lithium cells to prevent short-circuit.
Stage lead-acid in acid-rated containment; lithium in fire-separated, non-conductive bins with sand/quench provision (BFP Fire Code).
Log count/weight to the ledger per chemistry; issue incentive (W5350).
Monitor for swelling/thermal event; isolate any suspect cell in a quench container.

fields.Trigger: Customer returns spent fluorescent tubes, CFLs, or mercury-vapor lamps

workflows.name: Fluorescent, CFL & Mercury-Vapor Lamp Collection & Mercury Containment

Controls: - CTL-792 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Take-Back Operations — Collection, Handling & Reverse Logistics (PA-187.2).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-114 (DG), VS-78 (green building/clean-air adjacency)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Mercury-exposure risk**: a broken fluorescent releases mercury vapor in the store — a health and Clean Air Act (RA 8749) exposure; mitigated by mercury-tight rigid containers and a defined breakage/spill procedure (W5366).
- **Breakage-in-storage risk**: fragile lamps crushed in storage release mercury; mitigated by rigid containers and no-stacking rules.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste ledger (lamp stream); mercury-recycler scheduling; breakage-incident link (W5366).

steps.activity: Accept intact lamps only; broken lamps follow the spill/breakage procedure (W5366).
Place in mercury-tight lamp containers (rigid tubes/boxes) to prevent breakage and vapor release.
Log count/type to the ledger; issue incentive (W5350).
Store in the ventilated containment area away from customer access and stock.
Schedule pickup by the mercury/lamp recycler before container capacity (W5360).

fields.Participants: HSE Officer, FPA/DENR Partner, Compliance Specialist
fields.Trigger: Customer returns leftover pesticides, garden/agro chemicals, solvents, adhesives, thinners

workflows.name: Pesticide, Garden Chemical & Solvent Take-Back & Restricted-Substance Handling

Automation Opportunity: - Barcode auto-classifies compatibility group and restricted-substance status from the merchandise master.
Controls: - CTL-792 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Take-Back Operations — Collection, Handling & Reverse Logistics (PA-187.2).)
- operational: pesticide/solvent hazardous-waste handling; CTL-34 (FPA-restricted-substance compliance).
Cross-references: - links to VS-114 (DG), VS-24 (HSE), VS-145 (garden/chemical adjacency), VS-117 (DTI-BPS chemical standards)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Incompatible-mixing risk**: mixing incompatible chemicals (e.g. bleach and ammonia-based) in one cabinet causes reaction/fumes; mitigated by compatibility-group separation and labeling.
- **Restricted-substance risk**: mishandling FPA-controlled pesticides is a specific regulatory violation; mitigated by the restricted-substance protocol and FPA-licensed handlers.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste ledger (pesticide/solvent stream, by compatibility group); FPA/DENR handler scheduling; restricted-substance manifest flag.

steps.activity: Verify the container is labeled/identifiable; refuse unidentified/unlabeled chemicals (policy W5350).
Identify restricted/controlled pesticides (FPA-regulated) and route to the restricted-substance protocol (separate manifest, FPA-licensed handler).
Stage in the ventilated flame cabinet by compatibility group (no incompatible mixing); log to the ledger.
Issue incentive per policy (W5350).
Monitor cabinet fill; schedule pickup by the licensed chemical handler (W5360).

fields.Participants: HSE Officer, E-Waste Recycler Partner, Privacy/DPO (VS-91)
fields.Trigger: Customer returns used electronics, power tools, small appliances

workflows.name: Consumer E-Waste, Power Tool & Appliance Take-Back & Data-Bearing Device Sanitization

Automation Opportunity: - Data-device detection prompt at intake; sanitization certificate auto-generated and emailed.
Controls: - CTL-27: customer data safeguards / sanitization; CTL-41 (e-waste handling).
Cross-references: - links to VS-91 (privacy), VS-88 (records/sanitization cert), VS-143 (appliance haul-away), VS-99 (IT asset disposal), VS-155 (trade-in/resale cross-link)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Data-privacy risk**: recycling a customer's data-bearing device without sanitization breaches RA 10173 and exposes customer data; mitigated by mandatory sanitization + certificate.
- **Embedded-battery risk**: an e-waste unit with an undetected lithium battery causes a fire in the e-waste bin; mitigated by battery removal before staging.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste ledger (e-waste stream); data-sanitization certificate register (VS-91/VS-88); e-waste recycler scheduling (W5360).
Time Estimate: - ~15 min per visit (more if data device); ~250/yr/store → ~60 person-hours/yr/store.

steps.activity: Accept consumer e-waste/small appliances; route white-goods/large appliances to VS-143 haul-away/recovery.
Identify data-bearing devices (phones, tablets, smart tools, storage); route to data-sanitization before recycling (RA 10173).
Sanitize/destroy data-bearing media; issue a sanitization certificate to the customer.
Remove embedded batteries to the battery stream (W5355); log unit/count to the ledger.
Issue incentive per policy (W5350); stage for e-waste recycler pickup (W5360).

fields.Participants: LPG Program Lead (VS-175), HSE Officer, Cylinder Disposal Partner
fields.Trigger: Customer returns an unwanted/old/damaged LPG cylinder or it is condemned at the cage (VS-175)

workflows.name: Propane/LPG Cylinder Take-Back, Condemned-Cylinder Handling & Cross-link to VS-175

Automation Opportunity: - Cylinder barcode/ID scan auto-reconciles to the VS-175 fleet ledger and resolves deposit.
Controls: - CTL-100: cylinder-asset & deposit reconciliation; CTL-171 (condemned-cylinder hazardous-waste handling).
Cross-references: - links to VS-175 (propane/LPG program), VS-114 (DG), VS-24 (HSE/fire)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Pressurized-cylinder risk**: accepting a pressurized/valve-intact cylinder of unknown contents is a fire/explosion hazard; mitigated by the venting-verification gate and routing to the VS-175 protocol.
- **Cylinder-fleet-leakage risk**: take-back cylinders not reconciled to the VS-175 pool distort the deposit-float and asset ledger; mitigated by the cross-linked ledger and deposit resolution.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste ledger (cylinder stream) cross-linked to the VS-175 cylinder-fleet ledger; deposit/float resolution (VS-175).

steps.activity: Verify the cylinder is empty/vented before acceptance; refuse pressurized/valve-intact unknowns to the VS-175 venting protocol.
Inspect for condemnation criteria (rust, valve damage, out-of-test); route serviceable cylinders to the VS-175 pool, condemned to scrap.
Log the cylinder to the hazardous-waste/asset ledger (cross-link VS-175 cylinder fleet); resolve deposit/float if applicable.
Stage condemned cylinders in the BFP-rated cage (VS-175) for the disposal partner.
Coordinate pickup with the licensed cylinder-scrap partner (W5360).

fields.Participants: Store Staff, TSD Transporter (W5347), Compliance Specialist
fields.Trigger: Store stream-container fill threshold reached; scheduled pickup cycle

workflows.name: Hazardous Waste Consolidation, Manifest Generation & Licensed Transporter Pickup

Automation Opportunity: - Fill-threshold alerts auto-schedule pickup; manifest auto-generated and transporter-accredited at scheduling.
Controls: - CTL-792 (ensure controlled execution — Customer Take-Back Operations — Collection, Handling & Reverse Logistics (PA-187.2).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-114 (DG transport), VS-161 (TPRM transporter), VS-06 (logistics scheduling), VS-88 (manifest records retention)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-accumulation risk**: missing a pickup threshold leaves hazardous waste accumulating past permitted storage time/quantity (DENR-EMB limit); mitigated by threshold-based pickup alerts and scheduled cycles.

- **Manifest-handover risk**: releasing waste without a complete manifest breaks the chain-of-custody and BuildRight's cradle-to-grave liability; mitigated by a no-release-without-signed-manifest gate.
System Touchpoints: - Hazardous-waste manifest/chain-of-custody module (W5351); transporter-accreditation link; store ledger pickup-threshold alerts.
Time Estimate: - ~2 hours per pickup batch at store; ~60/store/yr → ~120 person-hours/yr/store.

steps.activity: Review the store hazardous-waste ledger; confirm containers at/over pickup threshold by stream.
Schedule the licensed transporter for the streams due; confirm transporter accreditation (W5347).
Generate the DENR-format manifest from the ledger (W5351); stage containers at the pickup point.
Hand over with transporter signature/timestamp and spill-response acknowledgment; release containers.
Confirm pickup in the ledger; track to TSD receipt (W5351 chain-of-custody); restage containment.
